design.algorithm: score = 0.40*skills + 0.20*assets + 0.20*district + 0.20*capital, each in [0,1]: skills = |founder ∩ card.skills_used| / max(1,|card.skills_used|) (untagged cards: capability overlap via skills.json at half weight); district = card.districts[d][0]/3, 0 if absent; capital = 1 if card band <= founder band, 0.5 one band above, excluded two or more above, 0.5 when unknown; motivation breaks ties (succession favours the prior trade). designs.understanding: The agent layer has no notion of 'what the conversation is waiting for'. AgentSession keeps only pending_slot (ideation.py:131), and _advance (ideation.py:846-873) is a chain of if-checks: yes/no only in CONFIRMING, every reply in GENERATING maps to Action('generate'), then skip, then OPINION, then slot observation. _offline_stream (655-700) then decides side effects (start research, wait, convene panel, build roadmap) by inspecting s.scan/s.roadmap/out flags. Because there is no explicit state, steps that need one have nowhere to live: after the roadmap every reply rebuilds the same headline (_roadmap_line, 902-909, 'costs or licences first?' with no route to either); a pending choice among cards or levers cannot be stored, resumed or matched against 'the second one'; the panel is convened on demand with scan=None (676-683) and narrates 'serious concerns' built on absent evidence; and the offline path awaits board.wait(research_wait_s=3.0) and, inside _absorb, council_wait_s=1.5 before its first sentence. All five flags hold at the cited lines. Root fix: a small explicit conversation state machine in the agent layer: a typed pending action stored in the session document, a pure decide() mapping (pending, utterance) to a transition, and guards on transitions (no panel before evidence, a spoken lead before any wait).

design.data_model: PendingAction (discriminator 'kind'): Ask{slot, question}; Confirm{objective}; Choose{choice:'card'|'lever', options:[Option{id, label, keywords[]}] (3-5), idea_version, offered_at_turn, represented:int}; Walk{section|None, offered:[str], cursor:int}; Idle. AgentSession.pending replaces pending_slot (from_dict upgrades old documents via T34) and gains opinion_requested: bool. Transition{pending, effects[], engine_action|None, reason}. Effect = StartResearch | ConvenePanel | BuildRoadmap | RebuildRoadmap(changed[]) | SpeakSection(name) | ApplyChoice(choice, option_id).
design.algorithm: decide(s, text) by s.pending.kind. ask: skip -> engine.skip; opinion -> keep Ask, add guarded ConvenePanel; else engine.observe(answering=slot) + engine.step. confirm: yes/no on word boundaries -> engine.confirm; accepted in EXPERIENCE mode before a card is chosen -> Choose(card) from T24's ranker; otherwise BuildRoadmap + Walk(offered=sections). choose: match_choice; Pick -> ApplyChoice (T24 card writeback or 1.2.4 lever patch, both bump idea_version via T06; a pick offered under an older version is refused and options re-presented); NoneOfThese -> T24 rule; Ambiguous/NoMatch -> re-present once, then ordinary observation so nobody is stuck. walk: route_section -> SpeakSection; a fact change reported by engine.observe (T03 put outcome 'changed') -> RebuildRoadmap, speak diff_line, continue the walk; 'done'/'thanks' -> Idle. Guards: ConvenePanel only if s.scan is set; if research is running set opinion_requested and say PANEL_AFTER_SEARCH; _absorb starts the panel after research when requested and its brief is narrated when ready; council.convene rejects scan=None as a backstop. Waits: any effect that waits on the board first yields a lead sentence (engine acknowledgement or SEARCHING); _absorb no longer waits for the panel.
design.interfaces: T03: engine.observe returns the put outcome so decide() can trigger RebuildRoadmap. T05: engine.step/Q_MAX unchanged, wrapped by decide(). T06: ApplyChoice bumps idea_version; Choose remembers its version. T24: ranked card options and writeback. T28: pending in ack and snapshot; replay skips decide(). T26: lead/walk sentences join the fixed list (recorded, translated); per-sentence language from T26. T34: format bump.
design.rollout: 1) PendingAction with an upgrade from pending_slot. 2) Move _advance into decide() with unchanged behaviour (golden tests on eval replays). 3) Guards and lead sentences. 4) Walk and revise. 5) Choose kinds land with T24 (card) and 1.2.4 (lever). One PR per step, merged by the owner.

designs.understanding: The turn stream is the main contract and is untyped at both ends: Python emits dicts via _event/_sse, the frontend has a hand-written AgentEvent union (agentClient.ts:78-86), and OpenAPI has no schema for any agent route. Nothing distinguishes a finished turn from a truncated one (streamTurn breaks on reader done, agentClient.ts:196-198); a save conflict is a 200 with an untyped 'error' after every sentence was spoken (routers/ideation.py:347-354); a replay after a drop between save and 'done' runs the turn twice (the stream route has no idempotency; 1.1.4.1 targets agent_turn, which the Talk page never calls); notices finished while disconnected are lost (board.notify only to current subscribers, jobs.py:110-113); a queued second utterance overwrites the first (Talk.tsx:153-155). All six flags hold. Fix: a typed event union with a terminal-event rule, client_turn_id with last_turn replay in the session document, typed error codes, result replay on subscribe and in the snapshot, and a client that enforces them.

design.algorithm: run_turn: lock; load (404 -> Error not_found, or expired when T07's store reports expiry); matching client_turn_id -> re-emit saved events with replayed=true, no decide(), no model call; else run turn_stream, set last_turn, save (VersionConflict -> Error conflict, retry=false), emit Done only after a successful save; exceptions -> Error failed, retry=true. Client: Done -> commit transcript; conflict -> drop the unsaved reply, reload snapshot, speak a fixed correction plus snapshot.pending's question; expired -> say so and offer a fresh start (no silent save(null)); no terminal event -> retry same id, dedupe by seq. Notices: on subscribe send board.take(research|council) first; the client replaces by 'at'.
